title: Sensex, Nifty End Flat as IT Gains Offset Metal Drag Ahead of Independence Day
excerpt: Markets closed marginally higher on August 14 as softer US inflation data boosted IT stocks, but geopolitical uncertainty and weak commodity prices kept broader gains in check.
body:
• Sensex closed at 80,597.66, up 57.75 points (0.07%), while Nifty 50 ended at 24,631.30, up 11.95 points (0.05%) on August 14
  • IT and pharma stocks led gains on softer US inflation data, while metals and energy dragged on falling commodity prices
  • S&P upgraded India's credit rating with a stable outlook, but geopolitical uncertainty ahead of the US-Russia summit kept investor sentiment cautious
  • Broader markets underperformed with mid-cap index down 0.3% and small-cap index down 0.4%

Indian equity markets ended marginally higher on Thursday, August 14, as cautious trading ahead of the US-Russia summit on Ukraine and the Independence Day holiday kept gains in check. The Sensex closed at 80,597.66, up 57.75 points or 0.07%, while the Nifty 50 settled at 24,631.30, up 11.95 points or 0.05%.

The session was volatile as it coincided with the weekly futures and options expiry. After opening flat, markets briefly dipped into the red before recovering on the back of buying in IT and pharma stocks. The broader market told a different story — the NSE Mid-cap index fell 0.3% and the Small-cap index declined 0.4%.

Five Factors That Shaped the Session

1. US Inflation Data and Fed Outlook: Softer-than-expected US inflation data released earlier in the week boosted hopes for Federal Reserve rate cuts, driving buying in export-oriented IT stocks. Wipro led the Nifty 50 gainers with a 2% advance, followed by Eternal (+1.71%) and Infosys (+1.50%).

2. Geopolitical Uncertainty: Investors remained cautious ahead of the scheduled US-Russia summit on the Ukraine conflict. Markets traded in a tight range as participants awaited clarity on geopolitical developments, with the potential for escalation keeping risk appetite subdued.

3. Trump Tariff Concerns: Renewed fears around trade tariffs added to the cautious tone. Gift Nifty signals earlier in the day reflected the uncertainty, with futures trading at a discount to the previous close.

4. S&P Credit Rating Upgrade: S&P's upgrade of India's sovereign credit rating with a stable outlook provided underlying support. The rating agency cited strong policy continuity and infrastructure-led growth as key factors, which analysts said would attract sustained foreign institutional investment over the medium term.

5. Commodity Prices and Sector Rotation: Crude oil holding above $80 per barrel weighed on energy stocks, while falling commodity prices hit metals hard. Tata Steel was the top Nifty loser, falling 2.81%, followed by Adani Ports (-1.38%) and Hero MotoCorp (-1.27%). Conversely, Consumer Durables was the top-performing sector, up 0.75%.

Market Breadth and Technical View

Market breadth was weak despite the headline index gains. Of 3,066 stocks traded on the NSE, 1,809 declined against 1,131 that advanced, with 104 unchanged. A total of 59 stocks hit 52-week highs — including Eternal, Apollo Hospitals, TVS Motor, InterGlobe Aviation, and Hyundai Motor — while 75 stocks touched 52-week lows.

"Nifty witnessed a lackluster trading session, remaining range-bound ahead of the Trump-Putin meeting on Friday. The overall sentiment is likely to favour bullish trades as long as the index holds above 24,337."

— Rupak De, Senior Technical Analyst, LKP Securities

What to Watch

Markets will be closed on Friday, August 15, for Independence Day. When trading resumes, the outcome of the US-Russia summit and any developments on the tariff front will set the tone. Analysts expect the S&P credit upgrade to provide medium-term support, but near-term direction will depend on global cues and foreign fund flows. Resistance for Nifty is placed at 24,660 and 24,850, while support lies at 24,337.
nri_angle: NRI investors tracking Indian equity markets and foreign fund flows will note the S&P credit upgrade and the impact of global geopolitical uncertainty on Indian equities ahead of the holiday-shortened week.
